one_liner: Rust interior-point solver for LP, QP, SOCP, SDP and exponential/power-cone problems; roughly ties ECOS on speed, solves far more QPs.
what_it_does: Solves convex problems of the form minimize 1/2 x'Px + q'x subject to Ax + s = b, s in a product of cones (zero, nonnegative, second-order, exponential, power, generalized power and, with the sdp feature, PSD cones). It is a Rust crate (clarabel on crates.io) with a Python extension (pip install clarabel), a C interface and a separate Julia implementation (Clarabel.jl). The interface is not a drop-in for ECOS: data goes in as CSC matrices with an explicit cone list, and you call DefaultSolver::new(P, q, A, b, cones, settings) then solve().
how_it_is_fast: It is a primal-dual interior-point method on a homogeneous embedding that keeps the quadratic term P in the KKT system instead of lifting it into a second-order-cone epigraph, as ECOS and other HSDE solvers must. QPs therefore stay QPs, with no extra cone and no Cholesky factor of P. Each iteration is a sparse quasidefinite LDL factorisation (a Rust QDLDL with AMD ordering by default; faer supernodal or Pardiso optional) after Ruiz-style equilibration and a presolve that drops rows whose bound is at or above 1e20.
when_to_use: Convex QPs where you need an interior-point answer at 1e-8 accuracy without reformulating the objective as an SOCP (the case where ECOS forces a Cholesky-based epigraph).
Mixed conic models (SOCP plus exponential or power cones) from CVXPY or similar modelling layers, where you want one open-source solver under Apache-2.0 instead of GPL ECOS.
Rust services or WebAssembly targets that need an embedded optimiser with no C toolchain; the default build pulls only pure-Rust crates.
Small and medium sparse problems (up to thousands of variables) solved once each; for repeated solves of a fixed-structure problem, use the update API with presolve disabled.
when_not_to_use: Pure QPs where speed is the goal: even in the 2023 qpbenchmark run, before the presolve bug, ProxQP had a 6.6x lower shifted-geometric-mean runtime on the dense subset and PIQP a 4.2x lower one on the full set, and against ECOS on the problems both solve Clarabel is roughly a tie (ECOS/Clarabel time 1.05 in 2023, 0.84 in 2024; derived from page data).

Low-accuracy, warm-started model-predictive-control loops: an ADMM solver (OSQP) or an active-set QP solver is usually cheaper per solve, and Clarabel takes no warm-start point (qpsolvers drops initvals; warm-start settings are open feature request #198).

Problems with explicit np.inf bounds on Clarabel 0.8.x or 0.9.x: their presolve panics when equality constraints and infinite-bound rows are mixed (issue #127, fixed in 0.10.0). Updating b with np.inf through solver.update still yields NumericalError in 0.11.1 (issue #218, open).
Badly scaled data: open issue #217 (0.11.1) reports false PrimalInfeasible and InsufficientProgress results on 8-variable QPs that solve once equilibration is turned off.
SDPs without a BLAS/LAPACK: the sdp feature needs one of the blas-src backends (OpenBLAS, MKL, Accelerate, netlib).

integration.form: crate (also a Python extension module built with maturin and a C API; cdylib)
integration.dependencies: amd, cfg-if, itertools, derive_builder, enum_dispatch, lazy_static, num-traits, thiserror (plus serde and serde_json in the default feature set); optional BLAS/LAPACK for SDP, faer for supernodal LDL, Pardiso (MKL or Panua)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.70 (rust-version in Cargo.toml for 0.11.x); Python wheels need Python 3.9+
integration.platforms: any Rust target including wasm; PyPI wheels for Linux x86-64 and aarch64, macOS x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for solver objects; a max_threads setting controls multithreaded KKT backends (faer, Pardiso), and the Python binding releases the GIL during solve (changelog 0.10.0, PR #122).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: CVXPY can switch solver=ECOS to solver=CLARABEL with the same model, but direct ECOS callers must rewrite G/h/A/b plus cone dimensions into Clarabel's single A, b and cone list.

gotchas: The 2024-09-07 qpbenchmark run used Clarabel 0.9.0, which contains the presolve panic its runner had reported two months earlier (Clarabel.rs #127, filed 2024-07-31, fixed in PR #137, released in 0.10.0 on 2025-02-02). qpsolvers 4.3.3 turns lb/ub = +-inf into inequality rows with h = inf, and qpbenchmark catches the exception as a failed solve. Across all 138 problems in results/qpbenchmark_results.csv, Clarabel solves 32 of 32 problems with all-finite variable bounds and 4 of 70 with both infinite bounds and equality constraints, so most of its 48% dense failure rate is this bug (derived from the repo's .mat files and CSV). In the 2023-08-30 run (qpbenchmark 1.1.0, Clarabel 0.5.1, same i7-6500U) it solved 96.8% of the dense subset and 89.9% of the full set.
Default verbose is true in the Rust DefaultSettings, so the solver prints its iteration log unless you turn it off.
Presolve (on by default) disables parametric data updates; an infinite b entry passed through solver.update is not clamped to get_infinity() = 1e20 and produces NaNs (issue #218).
If P is not upper-triangular the solver silently copies it to its upper triangle (problemdata.rs), so a non-symmetric P is not rejected.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling solves optimisation problems. The nearest are OrdinaryDiffEq.jl (replacing C/Fortran ODE codes) and hpla-rs (Rust sparse linear algebra on faer, which Clarabel can also use as its LDL backend). Pick Clarabel when the job is a convex conic or QP solve and you want a Rust or Python dependency rather than a C one.
verified_claims_summary: qpbenchmark (Maros-Meszaros dense subset, 62 problems, i7-6500U, PyPI builds called from Python through qpsolvers 4.3.3, run 2024-09-07) reports Clarabel 0.9.0 with a 6.1x lower shifted-geometric-mean runtime than ECOS 2.0.14. That gap comes entirely from failures charged at the 1000 s limit: ECOS fails because qpsolvers converts QPs to SOCPs, and Clarabel 0.9.0 fails on most infinite-bound problems because of presolve bug #127. On the 9 problems both solve, ECOS is about 1.19x faster in 2024 and Clarabel 0.5.1 about 1.05x faster in the 2023 run (derived from page data), so the measured speed is roughly a tie.
status_note: Apache-2.0 and widely used (about 2.17M crates.io downloads), but development has slowed: 0.11.1 (June 2025) is the latest release, only two commits have landed since (September 2025 and April 2026), and 26 issues are open, including RUSTSEC advisories against its pyo3 dependency.
